transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t stop noticing this crooked, swollen-looking side of my face, especially in the lesson videos. Once I see it, I just feel like the students, parents, and staff must be staring at that instead of hearing anything I’m saying.
Have family members, friends, or anyone else noticed or commented on this swelling, or do they see it differently?
I can’t stop seeing it myself, especially on the lesson videos. It looks crooked and swollen to me, and I just assume everyone watching is focused on that instead of what I’m teaching.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time repeatedly checking your face in mirrors or on your screen?

Yes. Before I post a lesson or join a parent conference, I keep adjusting the camera angle and replaying the video over and over. I’ll cover part of my face with my hand to see if it looks better, and sometimes I re-record the whole thing so many times that I miss prep work and end up late for class.

latest_inference.note: Patient exhibits classic features of Body Dysmorphic Disorder (classified under F45.2 in ICD-10): preoccupation with an imagined defect in appearance, repetitive checking behaviors (re-recording, checking angles), camouflaging, and functional impairment. F40.1, F22, and F42 are ruled out as the primary diagnosis.
